newsitem.title: USA: Intermediate funds like Memorial Hosp, Texas, deal.
newsitem.headline: Intermediate funds like Memorial Hosp, Texas, deal.

text.p: Strong demand for non-callable premium bonds helped Smith Barney Inc cut yields by five to 10 basis points in the midsection of Wednesday's $268 million Harris County, Texas, Memorial Hospital System deal.
"It went very well," an underwriting source familiar with the deal said, citing good demand from intermediate bond funds. Smith Barney cut yields between five to 10 basis points from 2007 to 2013.

"Because they were non-callable premium bonds, it was a very desirable feature, which is hard to find in today's new issue market," the underwriting source said. "We got (the issuer) a good price because of that."
The hospital revenue bond offering by the Harris County Health Facilities Development Corp featured a top yield of 5.77 percent in 2024, unchanged from the preliminary pricing.
County Debt Manager Terry Thornton said the county was "very happy," with the offering.
"It seemed like the deal went very quickly, and it seemed to be a very successful deal," Thornton said.
Approximately $40 million of the offering was sold to retail investors during a retail order period. "That's a nice size," Thornton said.
